Question: What is the primary purpose of a skip-to-content link (<a href="#main-content" class="skip-link">)?
Answer: It allows keyboard-only and screen-reader users to immediately bypass repetitive header navigation links and jump directly to the primary page content, satisfying WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks).

Question: How does the Accessibility Tree (A11y Tree) treat semantic HTML5 landmarks like <header>, <nav>, <main>, and <footer>?
Answer: It automatically assigns standard ARIA landmark roles: <header> becomes banner, <nav> becomes navigation, <main> becomes main, and <footer> becomes contentinfo. Screen reader users can jump directly between these regions using dedicated hotkeys.

Question: Why should every <section> tag have an aria-labelledby attribute pointing to its heading ID?
Answer: Without an accessible name, generic <section> elements are treated as plain containers in the accessibility tree. Adding aria-labelledby="title-id" elevates the section to an officially labeled landmark region that screen readers can index and announce.

Question: What is the purpose of aria-expanded and aria-controls on a mobile hamburger button?
Answer: aria-controls="nav-id" programmatically links the button to the mobile drawer element, while aria-expanded="false/true" informs assistive technologies whether the controlled drawer is currently open or collapsed.

Question: Why do we add role="list" to <ul> when using list-style: none in CSS?
Answer: WebKit (Safari/iOS) strips list semantics from the accessibility tree when list-style: none is applied in CSS. Explicitly adding role="list" restores the list announcement (e.g. "list, 4 items") for VoiceOver users.

Question: What is the performance advantage of placing <script src="app.js" defer> over placing scripts without defer in <head>?
Answer: defer downloads the script in parallel with HTML parsing and executes it in order ONLY after the HTML DOM is fully constructed (just before DOMContentLoaded), preventing JavaScript from blocking HTML tokenization.
